title: Epochal reserve reconciler and slip-window fairing for sustained-rate reservations
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: we continue to see oscillatory scale behavior when tenants alternate between short bursts and sustained ramps. Existing fractional reservation logic allocates strictly at request-time which causes unfair short-term giveaway and noisy autoscaler decisions. This PR introduces an epochal reservation reconciler and a slip-window fairing algorithm that smooths commitments across short epochs and provides proportional sustained-rate guarantees while preserving burst headroom. Implementation summary: add a light-weight epoch coordinator that buckets tenant reservations into fixed-duration epochs (default 30s) and reconciles desired commit volumes at epoch boundaries; introduce a slip-window fairing function that computes per-tenant credit allocations using a time-decayed moving average and a small tolerance window to allow short-term overshoots; implement a hedging mechanism that preserves a small cross-epoch safety buffer to avoid mid-epoch eviction thrash. The reconciler lives in pkg/fleet/reconciler and exposes a new ReservationEpoch API (internal), while the allocator is plumbed into the existing credit pool via a new CreditAllocator interface. Telemetry: new metrics added - fleet_epoch_duration_seconds, tenant_epoch_committed_tokens, tenant_slip_window_utilization, reserve_reconcile_latency_ms. Migration/compat: falling back to legacy reservation path if epoch coordinator disabled. Rollout plan: staged canary to 5% of dedicated fleets for 48h, followed by progressive rollout with automated regression checks on P95 latency and failed allocations. Tests: unit tests for allocator math, integration test simulating mixed burst + sustained workloads, and a canary harness script. Operational notes: default epoch length tuned after synthetic traces; operators can adjust epoch_length and slip_window_decay via Redwood Console and fleet config.

review_thread: Lena Rios (reviewer): What's the expected steady-state error between committed and observed throughput? We should document failure modes.
Aisha Khan (author): Expected steady-state error is bounded by slip_window_tolerance (default 5%). Added math and rationale to docs/ops/epochal-reservations.md and unit tests that assert bounds.
Marcus Chen (reviewer): How does this interact with tenant reserve preemption? Could hedging delay reclaim long enough to violate SLAs?

Aisha Khan (author): Hedging is sized as a small fraction (default 3% of epoch capacity) and only used when shortfalls are transient; added a safety circuit that forces reclaim if decline persists for 3 consecutive epochs. See allocator comments and tests.
Priya Patel (reviewer): CI integration looked flaky initially; confirm we won't regress autoscaler CPU overhead.
Aisha Khan (author): Optimized reconciliation loop to amortize allocations; CPU delta measured <1% for 1000-tenant synthetic run. Added benchmark and CI profile artifact link in PR description.
Lena Rios: Approving after docs and one small rename in allocator interface.
release_notes: Introduce epochal reservation reconciler and slip-window fairing to improve sustained-rate guarantees and reduce autoscaler oscillation. Config knobs: epoch_length, slip_window_decay, slip_window_tolerance. Backward-compatible with legacy reservation path. Operators should monitor tenant_slip_window_utilization after rollout.
notes_for_oncall: If allocations are unexpectedly failing after rollout, check metrics fleet_epoch_duration_seconds and tenant_epoch_committed_tokens for skew. To rollback: flip feature flag fleet.epochal_reservations.enabled=false and redeploy controller. Canary script is tools/canary/epochal_canary.sh.
changelog_entry: feature: epochal reservations and slip-window fairing for sustained-rate allocations (ops/configurable)
extra_context: Related work: complements recent proportional-reservation series; differs by operating on epoch boundaries and introducing a decay-based slip window to allocate cross-epoch credits more smoothly. See ENG-3412 for long-running benchmarks and ENG-3498 for customer incident that motivated hedging.
